headline: Nine-unit residential project at 101 and 105 Winter Street approved with conditions
summary: Earlier, members held a second workshop on a request to rezone part of 92 Cassidy Point Drive so Hearts of Pine could build a stadium there. Speakers gave mixed views, and several raised concerns about the working waterfront.
decisions: Approved driveway spacing of 23.43 feet and 36.92 feet at 101 and 105 Winter Street.
Approved a 5-inch curb reveal instead of the required 7 inches at 101 and 105 Winter Street.
Approved two driveways at 101 and 105 Winter Street, where the rules allow one.
Approved site plan for a nine-unit residential project at 101 and 105 Winter Street, with conditions.
Approved the planning board decision letter for 101 and 105 Winter Street.
discussion: Cassidy Point zoning limits: Members discussed a contract zone or an open space zone to limit other uses if a stadium was not built.
Working waterfront concerns: Concerns were raised about losing space for fishing, seafood, and cargo businesses. A market study found little demand for industrial use of the upland site.
Economic impact: Members said they wanted more information from the port authority and on past state and federal money in the area.
Winter Street design: A neighbor supported the design of the nine-unit project and said the empty lots had sat unused for a long time.
